verses.zh: 当春雨的时候，你们要向发闪电的耶和华求雨。他必为众人降下甘霖，使田园生长菜蔬。
verses.en: Ask the Lord for rain in the season of the late spring rains[NOTE:1]—the Lord who causes thunderstorms—and he will give everyone showers of rain and green growth in the field.
notes: Heb “the latter rain.” This expression refers to the last concentration of heavy rainfall in the spring of the year in Palestine, about March or April. Metaphorically and eschatologically (as here) the “latter rain” speaks of God’s outpouring of blessing in the end times (cf. Hos 6:3; Joel 2:21-25).

verses.zh: 因为，家神所言的是虚空；卜士所见的是虚假；做梦者所说的是假梦。他们白白地安慰人，所以众人如羊流离，因无牧人就受苦。
verses.en: For the household gods[NOTE:1] have spoken wickedness, the soothsayers have seen a lie, and the dreamers have disclosed emptiness and give comfort in vain. Therefore the people set out like sheep and become scattered because they have no shepherd.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew word תְּרָפִים (terafim, “teraphim”) refers to small images used as means of divination and in other occult practices (cf. Gen 31:19, 34-35; 1 Sam 19:13, 16; Hos 3:4). A number of English versions transliterate the Hebrew term (cf. ASV, NAB, NASB, NRSV) or simply use the generic term “idols” (so KJV, NIV, TEV).
Shepherd is a common OT metaphor for the king (see esp. Jer 2:8; 3:15; 10:21; 23:1-2; 50:6; Ezek 34).

verses.zh: 我的怒气向牧人发作；我必惩罚公山羊；因我―万军之耶和华眷顾自己的羊群，就是犹大家，必使他们如骏马在阵上。
verses.en: “I am enraged at the shepherds and will punish the lead goats.“For the Lord of Heaven’s Armies has brought blessing to his flock, the house of Judah, and will transform them into his majestic warhorse.

verses.zh: 房角石、钉子、争战的弓，和一切掌权的都从他而出。
verses.en: From him will come the cornerstone,[NOTE:1] the wall peg,[NOTE:2] the battle bow, and every ruler.[NOTE:3]
notes: On the NT use of the image of the cornerstone, see Luke 20:17; Eph 2:20; 1 Pet 2:6.

The metaphor of the wall peg (יָתֵד, yated), together with the others in this list, describes the remarkable change that will take place at the inauguration of God’s eschatological kingdom. Israel, formerly sheep-like, will be turned into a mighty warhorse. The peg refers to a wall hook (although frequently translated “tent peg,” but cf. ASV “nail”; TWOT 1:419) from which tools and weapons were suspended, but figuratively also to the promise of God upon which all of Israel’s hopes were hung (cf. Isa 22:15-25; Ezra 9:8).

This is not the usual word to describe a king of Israel or Judah (such as מֶלֶךְ, melekh, or נָשִׂיא, nasiʾ), but נוֹגֵשׂ, noges, “dictator” (cf. KJV “oppressor”). The author is asserting by this choice of wording that in the messianic age God’s rule will be by force.

verses.zh: 他们必如勇士在阵上将仇敌践踏在街上的泥土中。他们必争战，因为耶和华与他们同在；骑马的也必羞愧。
verses.en: And they will be like warriors trampling the mud of the streets in battle. They will fight, for the Lord will be with them, and will defeat the enemy cavalry.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the riders on horses will be put to shame,” figurative for the defeat of mounted troops. The word “enemy” in the translation is supplied from context.

verses.zh: 我要坚固犹大家，拯救约瑟家，要领他们归回。我要怜恤他们；他们必像未曾弃绝的一样，都因我是耶和华―他们的　神，我必应允他们的祷告。
verses.en: “I (says the Lord) will strengthen the kingdom[NOTE:1] of Judah and deliver the people of Joseph[NOTE:2] and will bring them back[NOTE:3] because of my compassion for them. They will be as though I had never rejected them, for I am the Lord their God, and therefore I will hear them.
notes: Joseph is mentioned here instead of the usual Israel (but see 2 Sam 19:20; Pss 78:67; 80:1; 81:5; Ezek 37:16; Amos 5:6, 15; 6:6) because of the exodus motif that follows in vv. 8-11.tn Or “the kingdom of Israel”; Heb “the house of Joseph.”
The anomalous MT reading וְחוֹשְׁבוֹתִים (vekhoshevotim) should probably be וַהֲשִׁי בוֹתִם (vahashi votim), the Hiphil perfect consecutive of שׁוּב (shuv), “return” (cf. Jer 12:15).

verses.zh: 以法莲人必如勇士；他们心中畅快如同喝酒；他们的儿女必看见而快活；他们的心必因耶和华喜乐。
verses.en: The Ephraimites will be like warriors and will rejoice as if they had drunk wine. Their children will see it and rejoice; they will celebrate in the things of the Lord.

verses.zh: 我要发嘶声，聚集他们，因我已经救赎他们。他们的人数必加增，如从前加增一样。
verses.en: I will signal for them and gather them, for I have already redeemed them; then they will become as numerous as they were before.

verses.zh: 我虽然（或译：必）播散他们在列国中，他们必在远方记念我。他们与儿女都必存活，且得归回。
verses.en: Though I scatter[NOTE:1] them among the nations, they will remember in far-off places—they and their children will survive and return.
notes: Or “sow” (so KJV, ASV). The imagery is taken from the sowing of seed by hand.

verses.zh: 我必再领他们出埃及地，招聚他们出亚述，领他们到基列和黎巴嫩；这地尚且不够他们居住。
verses.en: I will bring them back from Egypt and gather them from Assyria.[NOTE:1] I will bring them to the lands of Gilead and Lebanon, and there will not be enough room for them.
notes: I will bring them back from Egypt…from Assyria. The gathering of God’s people to their land in eschatological times will be like a reenactment of the exodus, but this time they will come from all over the world (cf. Isa 40:3-5; 43:1-7, 14-21; 48:20-22; 51:9-11).

verses.zh: 耶和华必经过苦海，击打海浪，使尼罗河的深处都枯干。亚述的骄傲必致卑微；埃及的权柄必然灭没。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] will cross the sea of storms and will calm its turbulence. The depths of the Nile will dry up, the pride of Assyria will be humbled, and the domination[NOTE:2] of Egypt will be no more.
notes: Heb “he,” in which case the referent is the Lord. This reading is followed by KJV, ASV, NAB (which renders it as first person), and NASB. The LXX reads “they,” referring to the Israelites themselves, a reading followed by many modern English versions (e.g., NIV, NRSV, TEV, NLT).
Heb “scepter,” referring by metonymy to the dominating rule of Egypt (cf. NLT).

verses.zh: 我必使他们倚靠我，得以坚固；一举一动必奉我的名。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: Thus I will strengthen them by my power,[NOTE:1] and they will walk about[NOTE:2] in my name,” says the Lord.
notes: Heb “I will strengthen them in the Lord.” Because of the perceived problem of the Lord saying he will strengthen the people “in the Lord,” both BHK and BHS suggest emending גִּבַּרְתִּים (gibbartim, “I will strengthen them”) to גְּבֻרָתָם (gevuratam, “their strength”). This is unnecessary, however, for the Lord frequently refers to himself in that manner (see Zech 2:11).

The LXX and Syriac presuppose יִתְהַלָּלוּ (yithallalu, “they will glory”) for יִתְהַלְּכוּ (yithallekhu, “they will walk about”). Since walking about is a common idiom in Zechariah (cf. 1:10, 11; 6:7 [3x]) to speak of dominion, and dominion is a major theme of the present passage, there is no reason to reject the MT reading, which is followed by most modern English versions.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter continues the same themes as chapter. 9. The time element is still ambiguous.

- Zechariah 10:4 and 11-12 are Messianic. Notice the capitalizations of NASB. The Aramaic Targums
also assert these verses as Messianic. However, others see

- Zech. 10:4 as referring to Judah

- Zech. 10:11-12 as referring to YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

- The theme of this chapter is the covenant people's dependence on YHWH, not Ba'al. This is the focus of Zech. 10:1.
Zechariah 10:2 shows the falsehood that Israel was depending on (cf. Hosea 11:3). The chapter concludes with an emphasis
on His people's victorious return in YHWH's name, not a fertility idol's name.

SPECIAL TOPIC; FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

- Notice the numbers of times the FIRST PERSON SINGULAR PRONOUN is used in chapters 9 and 10. YHWH
chooses to act Himself to accomplish His redempticve plans. These remind me of Ezek. 36:22-36, which describes the New Covenant
based on YHWH's actions, not human performance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ZECHARIAH 10:1-12

1Ask rain from the Lord at the time of the spring rain-

The Lord who makes the storm clouds;

And He will give them showers of rain, vegetation in the field to each man.

2For the teraphim speak iniquity,

And the diviners see lying visions

And tell false dreams;

They comfort in vain.

Therefore the people wander like sheep,

They are afflicted, because there is no shepherd.

3My anger is kindled against the shepherds,

And I will punish the male goats;

For the Lord of hosts has visited His flock, the house of Judah,

And will make them like His majestic horse in battle.

4From them will come the cornerstone,

From them the tent peg,

From them the bow of battle,

From them every ruler, all of them together.

5They will be as mighty men,

Treading down the enemy in the mire of the streets in battle;

And they will fight, for the Lord will be with them;

And the riders on horses will be put to shame.

6I will strengthen the house of Judah,

And I will save the house of Joseph,

And I will bring them back,

Because I have had compassion on them;

And they will be as though I had not rejected them,

For I am the Lord their God and I will answer them.

7Ephraim will be like a mighty man,

And their heart will be glad as if from wine;

Indeed, their children will see it and be glad,

Their heart will rejoice in the Lord.

8I will whistle for them to gather them together,

For I have redeemed them;

And they will be as numerous as they were before.

9When I scatter them among the peoples,

They will remember Me in far countries,

And they with their children will live and come back.

10I will bring them back from the land of Egypt

And gather them from Assyria;

And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon

Until no room can be found for them.

11And He will pass through the sea of distress

And strike the waves in the sea,

So that all the depths of the Nile will dry up;

And the pride of Assyria will be brought down

And the scepter of Egypt will depart.

12And I will strengthen them in the Lord,

And in His name they will walk," declares the Lord.

10:1 "Ask rain" This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 981, KB 1371). Rain was a gift
from God, e.g., Isa. 30:23; Jer. 10:13; Joel 2:23). The emphasis of Zech. 1:17; 9:17 is on social stability and
fruitfulness being from YHWH. Famine was part of the curse of Deuteronomy 28 (cf. Jer. 14:1-6), but abundant
rain was also part of the promised blessing if they followed God (cf. Deut. 11:13,14; 28:12). During Israel's
periods of idolatry (e.g., Hosea 4) she ascribed fertility to Ba'al (Canaanite storm and fertility god)
and not to YHWH (cf. Jer. 14:22). Chapter 10 highlights this grave mistake (cf. Zech. 14:17).

The VERB "ask" refers to prayer. This is theologically parallel to "seek." These acts
of repentant worship were done at YHWH's sanctuary. YHWH's people were not to "ask" and "seek" Ba'al but Him.
He and He alone was the provider of covenant promises, blessings!

▣ "at the time of the spring rain" In Palestine there are only two periods of rain
(cf. Deut. 11:14; Jer. 5:24; Joel 2:23).

- early rain at the autumn time before spring planting (October ‒ November)

- latter rain at the time of the maturing plant (March ‒ April)

Most regular moisture comes from the heavy dew. Because of the covenant promises and cursing
of Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29, these periods of rain became imagery for spiritual renewal and the presence of YHWH
with His people for blessing.

The "latter rains" became an idiom for YHWH's blessing in the end-time (e.g., Hosea 6:3;
Joel 2:23).

▣

NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB
"the storm clouds"

NKJV
"flashing clouds"

TEV
"rain clouds"

JPSOA
"storms"

The Hebrew word (BDB 304) is found twice in Job in contexts implying lightning
(Job 28:26; 38:15). The thrust of the passage is that YHWH controls the weather and, thereby, food
production and fertility (cf. Deut. 11:14-15), not Ba'al.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WATERS

10:2 "teraphim" This refers to household idols (BDB 1076; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 339), apparently in humanoid form,
used to discern the will of the departed family spirits or the family gods (cf. Gen. 31:19,34; Jdgs. 17:5; 18:14-20;
1 Sam. 15:23; 19:13; 2 Kgs. 23:24; Hosea 3:4). The exact etymology of this term (BDB 1076) is uncertain.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERAPHIM

▣

NASB, Peshitta
"speak iniquity"

NKJV. JPSOA
"speak delusion"

NRSV
"utter nonsense"

TEV
"nonsense"

NJB
"have talked nonsense"

REB
"utter empty promises"

LXX
"utter troubling things"

The VERB (BDB 180, KB 210) is a Piel PERFECT.

The NOUN (BDB 19) basically means "trouble," "sorrow," or "wickedness"
(cf. Num. 23:21; Ps. 10:7; 55:11; Isa. 10:1; 55:7; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 310-312). This Hebrew root has not been found in
Semitic cognate languages. Apparently, it is derived from the root for power (i.e., abuse of power).

- in worship ‒ 1 Sam. 15:22-23; Isa. 1:13; Hosea 4:15; 5:8; 10:5,8; Amos 5:5; Zech. 10:2

- in politics ‒ Isa. 31:2

- in law ‒ Isa. 10:1-2; 29:20-21

- in war ‒ Ps. 56:7

It is surprising that a list of idolatrous activities is mentioned in the post-exilic period (cf. Mal. 3:5). This whole
chapter may be an allusion to Moses' prophecy in Deut. 4:25-31.

▣ "the diviners see lying visions" This is a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE
(BDB 890, KB 1115, "the ones divining") plus a Qal PERFECT VERB (BDB 302, KB 301,
"see lies"). Most of these false methods of attempting to find the will of God are mentioned in
Deut. 18:9-13, esp. Deut. 18:10 (cf. 2 Kgs. 17:17). Divining is especially mentioned in 1 Sam. 15:23. It
either refers to natural (e.g., flight of birds, clouds, sheep livers) or manmade (e.g., casting sticks,
tea leaves) means of determining the will of deity (cf. Ezek. 21:21). Here, this term (BDB 890) refers to
false prophets (cf. Isa. 3:2; Jer. 27:9; 29:8; Ezek. 13:9,23; 22:38; Micah 3:11).

For a good discussion of "divination" see New International Dictionary of Old Testament
Theology and Exegesis, vol. 3, pp. 945-951 or Zondervan's Pictorial Encyclopedia of The Bible,
vol. 2, pp. 146-149.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

▣ "And tell false dreams" The VERB (BDB 180, KB 210) is a Piel
IMPERFECT. YHWH did often speak through dreams.

- Jacob, Gen. 28

- Joseph, Gen. 37:39-41

- Daniel, Dan. 1:17; 2:4,7

However, sometimes dreams were simply manipulative lies or imaginations of the
human subconscious (e.g., Deut. 13:1-5; Jer. 23:32; 27:9-10; 29:8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣ "They comfort in vain" The VERB (BDB 636, KB 688) is also a Piel
IMPERFECT. The NOUN (BDB 210 I; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 1003-1004) "vain," or
"empty," so common in Ecclesiastes (see full note at Eccl. 1:2), is the same root as "idol" (cf. 2 Kgs. 17:15;
Jer. 23:32; 27:9,10). They are nothing, just figments of human superstition and fear, as is this false hope from false prophets!

SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE,
NOTHINGNESS

▣ "Therefore the people wander like sheep" The VERB (BDB 652 I, KB 704)
is a Qal PERFECT. The term "the people" is in italics, which shows that it is not
in the Hebrew text. This verse could refer to the religions leaders, the people, or both. The classic
prophetic text about false shepherds and God's flock is in Ezekiel 34, but also is used often by Jeremiah
(cf. Jer. 2:8; 10:21; 23:1-2; 50:6).

▣ "They are afflicted, because there is no shepherd" This is a Qal IMPERFECT
VERB (BDB 776 III, KB 853) followed by a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, "shepherding"
(BDB 944 I, KB 1258). The concept of shepherd as a title for kings is very common in the ANE
(cf. Baldwin, Tyndale Old Testament Commentaries, pp. 171-172). The king often stands as a
representative of the national god. YHWH is often spoken of as shepherd and His people as sheep
(cf. Gen. 49:24; Num. 27:17; Ps. 23:1-2; Isa. 40:11; Ezek. 34:12).

This discussion of a divine shepherd sets the stage for chapters 11-13. Zechariah is unique
in his imagery of a wounded shepherd (cf. Zech. 12:10; 13:7), which is theologically parallel to the
Suffering Servant of Isaiah 53 (the same Hebrew term, "afflicted" (BDB 776 III) is used in Isa. 53:4,7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SUFFERING MESSIAH

10:3 "My anger is kindled against the shepherds" This is another Qal ACTIVE
PARTICIPLE (BDB 944 I, KB 1258) and a Qal PERFECT VERB (BDB 354, KB 351),
"is hot." In Ezekiel 34 (esp. Ezek. 34:17) YHWH also condemns His covenant people's civil and religious
leaders for their lack of faithfulness to Him.

The term "male goats" may refer to foreign leaders (TEV, cf. Zech. 10:11; Isa. 14:9; Jer. 51:40).

▣ "For the Lord of hosts" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"has visited"

NRSV, REB
"cares for"

TEV
"will take care of them"

NJB
"comes to visit"

JPSOA
"taken thought"

LXX
"will have concern"

The Hebrew VERB (BDB 823, KB 955, Qal IMPERFECT)
means "visited"

- for blessing, cf. Zech. 10:3c; Gen. 50:24; Exod. 3:16; 4:31; 13:19

- for judgment, cf. Zech. 10:36; 1 Sam. 15:2; Lam. 4:22; Hosea 8:13; 9:9). The best parallel passage is Jer. 23:2. In
Zech. 11:16 God allows an evil shepherd to decimate the flock.

▣ "His flock, the house of Judah" This refers to the southern tribes of Judah, Benjamin,
Simeon, and most of the tribe of Levi.

The northern remaining tribes were known as

- "Israel" (collective name)

- Ephraim (largest tribe)

- Samaria (the capital city)

This tribal split occurred in 922 B.C. (cf. 1 Kgs. 11:9-13,26-40).

In this chapter Judah is mentioned in Zech. 10:3 and Ephraim in 10:7. This prophet emphasizes
their reunification (cf. Zech. 10:6a,b). The post exilic community and the eschatological will be one people
(cf. Zech. 10:4d; 6a,b; 8:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "And will make them like His majestic horse in battle" The VERB
(BDB 962 I, KB 1321) is a Qal PERFECT with waw. The term "majestic" (BDB 217 I)
is used to describe horses in Job 39:19-25, esp. v. 20. This same word is used in Zech. 6:13 for the majesty
of the coming king, but here of His war mount. These are images for YHWH's people being used
(cf. Jer. 51:20-33) and honored by His Messiah when He returns to rule and reign.

YHWH is transforming and equipping His people so as to change them from sheep (or devious
"he goats") into majestic war stallions (cf. Zech. 9:13). This is an example of the drastic contrasts in
prophetic literature (e.g., no war in Zech. 9:10 vs. war in Zech. 9:13; 10:3).

10:4 "From them" The Masoretic Text has "from him" (cf. NKJV, Rotherham, and NAB, also note "He" of
Zech. 10:11). There have been several possibilities as to the object of this verse:

- it refers to future events, either Maccabean (Selucid) or eschatological

- it is a direct reference, which means out of Judah leaders will come (NIV, cf. Zech. 10:3-6;
Gen. 49:10; 2 Samuel 7)

- the Targums, which are Aramaic translations and interpretations of the Hebrew text, assert
that this refers to King Messiah

Notice how YHWH rejects the current leadership who seek information from other places than YHWH
(i.e., teraphim, diviners, dreamers) but now He will restore godly, faithful leaders symbolized by

- cornerstone (BDB 819)

- tent peg (BDB 450)

- bow (BDB 905 CONSTRUCT 536)

- ruler (BDB 481)

▣ "the cornerstone" This (BDB 819, FEMININE SINGULAR NOUN) refers to the Messiah
in Ps. 118:22 and Isa. 28:16 (also FEMININE SINGULAR).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CORNERSTONE

▣ "tent-peg" This Hebrew term (BDB 450) is used of three kinds of pegs.

- for tents (cf. Jdgs. 4:21; 5:26; Isa. 33:20; 54:2)

- for hanging things on (cf. Isa. 22:22-24; Ezek. 15:3)

- for building the tabernacle (cf. Exod. 27:19; 35:18; 38:20,31)

The point of the imagery is

- holding ability and thereby permanence (cf. Ezra 9:8; Isa. 22:23)

- an ANE sign of the completion of a temple (see IVP Bible Background Commentary [OT], p. 806)

Therefore, the cornerstone was the beginning and the peg the completion.

▣ "the bow of battle" This is a military idiom (cf. Zech. 9:10; Exod. 15:5). The imagery
of this verse speak of stability, victory, and unified leadership.

▣ "ruler" This is literally "oppressor." This is the very same Hebrew word (BDB 620) which
is used in Zech. 9:8 in a negative sense. However, it seems to be used in a positive sense here
(cf. Isa. 60:17) for the administrative or military leaders at the inauguration of the reign of the
coming Messiah (cf. Isaiah 9).

10:5 "Treading down the enemy in the mire of the streets in battle" "Treading down" (BDB 100,
KB 115, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 619), possibly "trampling." As YHWH
"tramples down" His enemies (i.e., Isa. 14:19,25; 63:6; Ps. 60:12), He empowers His people to trample their enemies
(cf. Ps. 44:5; 108:13).

This phrase is a standard idiom of defeat (cf. 2 Sam. 22:43). However, in this context where rain is
mentioned (cf. Zech. 10:1) it may refer to mud caused by YHWH's special presence (cf. Jdg. 4-5).

The term "streets" (BDB 299) means "outside streets," which seems to refer to an open
market (e.g., Zech. 9:3; 10:5; Isa. 5:25; 10:6; 15:3; 24:11; 51:20,23; Jer. 5:1;7:17,34; 37:21;
Ezek. 11:6; 28:23).

▣ "they will fight, for the Lord will be with them"
Zechariah 9:1-10 shows that YHWH would do the fighting, but Zech. 9:13-16 and Zech. 10:3-7 seem to say
that the Israelites would do the fighting (BDB 535, KB 526 Niphal PERFECT), but with
Him in their midst (cf. Jer. 51:20-23).

▣ "the riders on horses will be put to shame" YHWH turns His people into majestic war horses
(cf. Zech. 10:3d), but the war horses of the enemies are defeated (BDB 101, KB 116 Hiphil
PERFECT with waw, cf. Amos 2:15; Hag. 2:22).

The VERB (i.e., "put to shame," BDB 101, KB 116, Hiphil PERFECT
with waw; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 624) is used often of a defeated army (2 Kgs. 19:26; Isa. 19:9; 37:27; 41:11; Jer. 46:24;
48:20; Ezek. 32:30; Micah 7:16). Remember, in the ANE the defeat and humiliation of a national army meant the humiliation of
that nation's deity.

10:6 Notice the parallelism in the first two lines. YHWH will unify His people (i.e., "Judah" and
"Joseph"). Also notice the parallelism of the VERBAL form in which the FIRST PERSON
PRONOUN "I" is highlighted in the first three lines. His people are "strengthened" (BDB 149, KB 175
Piel PERFECT with waw) and "saved" (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil
IMPERFECT) because He acts (i.e., Ezek. 36:22-36)! The entire verse reflects His sovereignty, past, present, and
future.

Zechariah speaks of YHWH's salvation and deliverance

- from the Exile (cf. Zech. 8:7)

- from cursing to blessing (Zech. 8:13)

- unto an eschatological triumph (cf. Zech. 9:9; 10:6; 12:7)

▣ "Joseph" This is another way of referring to the northern tribes known as Israel, Ephraim
(Zech. 10:7), and Samaria.

▣ "I shall bring them back" This word (BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil PERFECT with
waw; see NET Bible, p. 1674, #5) is a combination of (BDB 998), "bring them back" (NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB,
cf. Zech. 10:10) and "make them dwell" (BDB 442, cf. NASB footnote and Zech. 10:4), which is the translation of the
Septuagint. Many rabbis assert that the form is definitely ambiguous so as to emphasize both elements
(i.e., repentance and permanent residence in the Promised Land).

NASB, NRSV
"Because I have had compassion on them"

NKJV, Peshitta
"because I have mercy on them"

"I will have compassion on them"

NJB
"because I have taken pity on them"

"in my compassion for them"

This Hebrew VERB (BDB 933, KB 1216, Piel PERFECT) is
used often for YHWH's compassion on His people (cf. Exod. 33:19; Deut. 30:3; 2 Kgs. 13:23; Isa. 14:1; 30:18;
49:10,13; 54:8,10; 55:7; 60:10; Jer. 12:15; 30:18; 31:20; 33:26; Hosea 1:6-7; 2:19,23; Micah 7:18-20). This
word assured them that YHWH had reestablished the covenant with all of its benefits (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 28). They had
experienced the curses!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "they will be as though I had not rejected them" This verse surely speaks of YHWH's forgiveness
and restoration, but it also denotes that He broke the covenant because of His people's sins. It is so
difficult to talk about the mercy and forgiveness of YHWH while at the same time reminding humans that the
covenant is conditional. He desires fellowship with a holy people. He wants a holy people to reflect His
character to a lost world. The old covenant was performance based (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 27-29), but fallen humans
were incapable of obedience (cf. Romans 7 and Galatians 3). Therefore, the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34;
Ezek. 36:22-38) is based on

- the gracious, unchanging character of YHWH (cf. Mal. 3:6)

- the work of the Messiah

- the drawing power of the Spirit (cf. John 6:44,65)

The goal is still a righteous people, but the mechanism of that righteousness has changed.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRISTIAN ASSURANCE

▣ "For I am the Lord their God, and I will answer them" The covenant
title is made up of the names for Israel's Deity.

- YHWH, used in Gen. 2:4 ‒ see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

- Elohim used in Gen. 1:1 ‒ see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

These covenant terms emphasize the restoration of the covenant relationship. Answered prayer (BDB 772 I, KB 851,
Qal IMPERFECT) is one of the benefits. The broken covenant is illustrated in Zech. 7:13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

10:7 "Ephraim will be like a mighty man" The northern ten tribes, so devastated by exile, will be
reunited with Judah into one family. The term "mighty" (BDB 150) is used of Judah's men in Zech. 10:5.

▣ "their heart will be glad as if from wine" Psalm 104:15 says that wine is a gift from
God to gladden the hearts of men. In Zech. 9:15 it described victorious soldiers. Here it is also imagery
for joy in military victory provided by YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES
TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOL ABUSE

▣ "their children will see it and be glad" This speaks of social stability and peace, as
does Zech. 9:17.

▣ "Their hearts will rejoice in the Lord" This same VERB
(BDB 162, KB 189, Qal JUSSIVE; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 955) was used in Zech. 9:9 (Qal IMPERATIVE)
at the coming of YHWH. In this verse the root is used of exalting in Him and His acts of deliverance and reestablishment
of His people. This verse may be an allusion to Isa. 41:16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

10:8 "I will whistle for them" This (Qal IMPERFECT COHORTATIVE) refers to a
characteristic call or sound (i.e., piping) of the shepherd gathering (second VERB, "gather"
[BDB 867, KB 1062] is a Piel IMPERFECT used as a COHORTATIVE) his
sheep (cf. Jdgs. 5:16). The exact sound is uncertain (BDB 1056, KB 1656), but it is an allusion to YHWH's
gathering His scattered people (cf. Isa. 5:26; 7:18,19).

▣ "I have redeemed them" This Hebrew term (BDB 804, KB 911 Qal PERFECT)
means to buy back or ransom. Here it is used of YHWH's activity of restoring His people to the Promised Land
(cf. Jer. 31:11). Jeremiah 31:10-13 may be the background to Zech. 9:17. Zechariah uses many phrases and
terminologies from Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and the Minor Prophets before his day.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

▣ "they will be as numerous as they were before" This context is reminiscent of Jer. 30:18-22.
Not only will the remnant return, but YHWH will restore the full number of residents (cf. Ezek. 36:37-38).

One of God's promises to the Patriarchs was that their descendants would be numerous
(cf. Gen. 13:16; 15:5; 22:17; 26:4; 28:14; 32:12; Num. 23:10).

10:9 "I scatter them" This context emphasizes the sovereignty of YHWH over history and redemption
(cf. Zech. 10:3,6,9,10; Deut. 4:27; 28:64). He acts in blessing and cursing (cf. Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29) based on His people's
obedience to the Mosaic covenant. But even amidst disobedience, He still acts in faithfulness to His own
character and purpose (cf. Jer. 31:27-28).

The Hebrew term "scatter" (BDB 281, KB 282, Qal IMPERFECT) can mean
"sow" (NKJV). YHWH sowed them because of their idolatry and faithlessness to His covenant (cf. Ezek. 6:9-10),
but after judgment they will remember Him and be faithful to Him and teach their children about Him (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25;
11:19; 32:46. This was YHWH's plan for taking His message to the world. Often acts of judgment turn into blessings:

- the dispersion after the tower of Babel in Genesis 10-11 caused nationalism, which protects
humanity from a one-world government

- the wilderness wandering period was due to their unbelief, but YHWH turned it into a unique time
of His personal care, provision, and presence with His people

- Calvary looked so evil and hateful, but God used it for universal redemption

- the persecution of the early church resulted in world-wide gospel proclamation (cf. Acts 8:4)

His people did not reach out so He sowed them into the world that He might bring them and others
(cf. Zech. 8:20-23) back with them to Himself (see Solomon's prayer in 1 Kings 8, especially vv. 43 and 60)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "they will remember Me" The VERB (BDB 269, KB 269) is a Qal
IMPERFECT. This reminds one of Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple
(cf. 1 Kgs. 8:46-53). Note the personal element "remember Me," not just the stipulations. Both are part
of the covenant relationship.

YHWH's people are to remember what He has done for them (i.e., the Exodus and Conquest) and
trust Him in the present difficulties. He acts according to His unchanging, gracious character. Even His judgment
is an act of mercy (i.e., Exile).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

The MT has "and they shall live" (BDB 310, KB 309, Qal PERFECT
with waw). The UBS Text Project, p. 415, suggests a change of vowels to "and they shall rear," but
with a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

10:10 "Egypt. . .Assyria" These were the ancient enemies of Israel used to symbolize all of the
enemies of YHWH's people.

▣ "the land of Gilead" This was a famous pasture land (cf. Jer. 22:6; 50:19) on the east side
of Jordan above the Jabbok River. It was known for its cattle and medicine (cf. Jer. 8:22; 46:11).

▣ "Lebanon" This refers to the realm of Hiram, later called Phoenicia. It was famous for its
artisans and lumber (cf. 1 Kgs. 4:33; 5:6,9,14; 7:2; 16:17,21; Isa. 35:2). It was a place of famed beauty
and fertility (cf. Sol. 4:8,11,15; 5:15; 7:4). It is included in the Promised Land in Deut. 1:7; 11:24 and
Joshua 1:4.

▣ "Until no room can be found for them" This is an idiom of abundance. The Promised Land
will be completely filled with YHWH's faithful people.

This multiplication of inhabitants (especially children, cf. Zech. 10:7c) is also mentioned
in Isa. 49:14-21 and 54:1-3.

10:11

NASB
"He will pass through the sea of distress"

NKJV, Peshitta
"He shall pass through the sea with affliction"

NRSV
"They shall pass through the sea of distress"

TEV
"When they pass through their sea of trouble"

NJB
"they will cross the sea of Egypt"

REB
"They will pass through the sea of Egypt"

JPSOA
"Ahemmede in force shall pass over the sea"

LXX
"They shall pass through a narrow sea"

As is so common to prophetic and apocalyptic literature, the subject and mood change
without notice or textual markers. This is especially true of this context in Zechariah. See Contextual
Insights at the beginning of chapter 9.

The problem is trying to find the SUBJECT and OBJECT of
Zech. 10:11 and 12. Some assert that

- it is the returnees because of Zech. 10:10, "they," LXX

- it is the Messiah (MT, "he")

- it is YHWH (cf. Zech. 10:12; Isa. 43:2, The Pulpit Commentary, Zechariah, vol. 14, p. 108)
and is an allusion to the Exodus (cf. JB and RSV translations)

- In my opinion, because Zech. 10:12 implies YHWH and another person ("he"), I believe that these
verses are Messianic.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOCALYPTIC LITERATURE

▣ "So that all the depths of the Nile will dry up" This is surely a historical allusion to the
crossing of the Red Sea (cf. Exod. 15:5) and Jordan Rivers. These were mighty acts of provision. The return
from Exile is depicted in the same way (cf. Isa. 44:27). Eschatologically YHWH removes all natural barriers
to Himself: rivers, valleys, mountains, as a symbol of a full and free access.

▣ "the pride of Assyria" See note at Zech. 9:6.

10:12 "in His name" Zechariah 10:1 begins by saying they were to pray for rain from YHWH, as they had
previously been praying to idols. Zechariah 10:12 concludes this thought by asserting that they would walk
in YHWH's name and not in the idol's name (cf. Micah 4:5).

Both VERBS

- strengthen ‒ BDB 149, KB 175, Piel PERFECT with waw

- walk ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Hithpael IMPERFECT

speak of YHWH's power and presence allowing His people to possess, control, and fully enjoy
the Promised Land again (i.e., Micah 4:5).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the time element of this chapter? (past, present, near future, or end-time) Why?

- Does Zech. 10:2 ever describe the life of the Jewish nation? If so, when?

- Why is God called "shepherd" and His people sheep?

- List the Messianic references of this chapter.

- How and when will Judah and Ephraim be reunited?
